title: MCP server (exasol-mcp-server)
tagline: The read-only bridge between your AI client and the database.
role: Your AI client starts this server on demand over stdio and queries the database through it. It connects as a dedicated mcp_readonly user, so reads work everywhere and writes are rejected by the database itself - not by client-side filtering.
boundary: Prove the boundary, do not assert it: as the MCP user, SELECT PRIVILEGE FROM SYS.EXA_USER_SYS_PRIVS returns exactly CREATE SESSION, SELECT ANY TABLE, USE ANY SCHEMA.

quickstart.note: Then look for an MCP server named exasol. Claude Code and Gemini CLI can also run /mcp in an existing session.

commands.summary: Configure MCP in supported AI clients.
commands.description: Backs up each config first, then writes the managed entries: exasol always, plus dash-server when that add-on is installed.

commands.summary: Which clients are managed, and where.

commands.description: This is what the AI client runs; you rarely run it by hand.

commands.summary: Run the server in HTTP mode instead of stdio.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS
environment.effect: Which clients to configure, by name. Never menu numbers.

notes: The database credential is stored as plaintext in each client's configuration file. It is the read-only user's password, not the admin one.

troubleshooting.symptom: The assistant cannot see the database
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit status first, then exakit mcp-doctor, then restart the AI client.
The database is not running: exakit start.

troubleshooting.symptom: The exasol server is missing after setup
troubleshooting.remedy: The client was not restarted. Restart it, or run /mcp in Claude Code or Gemini CLI.
